title: A comprehensive guide to research protocols for collecting and coding thoughts
author: Barzykowski, Ilczuk, et al.

steps.title: Recruit participants
steps.instruction: Recruit 240 young adults aged 18–35 years, offering a reward of PLN 50 (≈ $13). Advertise the study as a “study investigating the focus of attention” so participants are unaware of the spontaneous‑thought focus. Randomly assign each participant to one of three conditions: control (no working‑memory load), low load, or high load.

steps.title: Prepare computer stations
steps.instruction: Set up individual computer stations in a controlled laboratory. Test participants in groups of 2–12 people, each using a separate station.

steps.title: Affix keyboard markers
steps.instruction: Place a red square on the “m” key of each keyboard to simplify response selection.

steps.title: Load vigilance task program
steps.instruction: Open the Unity‑based vigilance‑task program on each computer.

steps.title: Configure task parameters
steps.instruction: Set the task to display 785 slides total, of which 15 are infrequent target slides containing vertical lines (all others show horizontal‑line patterns). Program the presentation of 270 short verbal phrases throughout the task and schedule 23 random thought‑probe interruptions.

steps.title: Run vigilance task
steps.instruction: Instruct participants to identify the 15 target slides while the remaining slides appear. During the task, present the 270 phrases and, at 23 random intervals, pause the task and ask participants to report the thought they were having and whether it was spontaneous or deliberate.

steps.title: Collect thought descriptions
steps.instruction: After the vigilance segment (average duration 1 h 15 min), present each recorded thought one by one on the screen and ask participants to indicate whether the thought referred to a past memory or a future event.

steps.title: Optional working‑memory load modification
steps.instruction: If using the experimental load condition, display a 1.5 cm × 1.5 cm square in the centre of the screen on each trial containing a random consonant (B, C, D, F, G, H, K, M, N, P, R, S, T, W, Z). Show each letter for 2 s with a 0.5 s inter‑stimulus interval. Instruct participants to press the green button (“X” key) whenever the current letter matches the one presented 1 trial ago (low‑load) or 3 trials ago (high‑load).

steps.title: Code collected thoughts
steps.instruction: Have expert judges code the post‑task thought descriptions to identify involuntary autobiographical memories (IAMs) and involuntary future thoughts (IFTs).
